title: Adaptive KV-prefetch rate limiter for realtime console metrics pipeline
creator: Asha Rangan
description:
Problem:
The console telemetry ingest pipeline experiences sporadic tail-latency spikes when tenant traffic contains high-cardinality hotkeys (heavy repeat prefixes) and long KV cache misses. Our existing prefetching and batching heuristics are static and tuned for average cases, causing either excessive upstream load (over-prefetch) or increased token latency (under-prefetch) during bursty tenant behavior.

Goal:
Build an adaptive rate limiter that controls KV-prefetch concurrency and prefetch window size per-tenant (and per-route) in real time. The operator should dynamically balance throughput and per-request P99 latency while protecting upstream model-serving pools and KV backends from amplification during hotkey storms. It must be lightweight, observable, and safe to roll out as a canary.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change model routing or batching algorithms outside of prefetch concurrency controls.
- Not implementing new KV cache formats or replacing the cache store.

Design considerations and constraints:
1) Per-tenant policy: Respect per-tenant SLAs and quota limits. Default policy is conservative for free-tier tenants and more aggressive for dedicated tenants.
2) Feedback signals: Use real-time signals: request queue depth, per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latency, KV miss ratio, backend error rate, and recent prefetch success rate.
3) Controller loop: A low-frequency control loop (100-500ms) should adjust two knobs: concurrent prefetch permits and prefetch lookahead window (in tokens/chunks). Use exponential backoff when errors/failures spike.
4) Safety: Global circuit breaker for system-wide overload; per-tenant fallback to simplified on-demand prefetch if operator is unhealthy.
5) Observability: Expose metrics for permits granted, throttled requests, prefetch hit/miss, control loop decisions, and changelog events. Add tracing tags for per-request adjudication.
6) Rollout: Support canary by tenant group and feature flag via Console. Must be toggleable with no schema changes.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (spike): Implement control loop as a stream processor stage in the ingest pipeline that consumes telemetry windows and emits permit adjustments. Prototype as a sidecar operator using existing stream consumer interface. (2w)
- Phase 2 (integration): Wire operator to prefetch path; add token-bucket style permit checks before issuing prefetches. Add basic Prometheus metrics + logs. (2w)
- Phase 3 (safety + rollout): Implement per-tenant policies, circuit-breaker, and feature-flagged rollout. Run canary against 5% traffic from internal staging tenants. (1w)
- Phase 4 (observability and tuning): Collect 2 weeks of telemetry, run automated load tests with synthetic hotkey patterns, and tune heuristics. Ship initial policy defaults. (2w)

Benchmarks and success criteria:
- Reduce P99 prefetch-induced latency by >= 35% for heavy-hotkey tenants under synthetic test.
- Avoid increasing upstream KV request rate by more than 10% for average tenants.
- No regression in baseline throughput for dedicated tenants.

Artifacts and links:
- Spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console-ingest/kv-prefetch-spike (doc)
- Load test harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-loadtests/pull/124
- Draft design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-prefetch-design

Open decisions:
- Control loop frequency tradeoff: 100ms offers faster adaptation but increases control noise; 500ms reduces churn. Team proposal: start at 250ms with smoothing window.
- Metric aggregation window size for per-tenant signals: default 30s with outlier clamping.

Risks:
- Adaptive controller oscillation causing thrashing; mitigated with hysteresis and minimum hold time for adjustments.
- Misconfiguration could starve low-priority tenants; mitigated via safe defaults and explicit per-tenant caps.

Next steps:
- Complete spike implementation and run internal A/B tests on staging.
- Create follow-up tickets for UI knobs in Console and for SRE runbook updates.
